target.title: fix(memory): keep batch failure attempts finite
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`recordMemoryBatchFailure` used `Math.max(1, attempts)`, so malformed non-finite values such as `NaN` could poison the failure counter. Once `count` became `NaN`, the disable threshold was never reached.

## Why This Change Was Made

Failure attempts are now normalized to positive safe integers. Malformed, non-finite, fractional, or unsafe values fall back to one failed attempt.

## User Impact

Memory batching can still disable itself after repeated failures even when malformed attempt metadata reaches the state update path.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-vitest-cache-memory-batch-rebase node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-batch-state.test.ts`
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-batch-state.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-batch-state.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- Claude autoreview: clean after rebase to `upstream/main`

## Proof

The regression tests prove `NaN` no longer poisons the counter and `Infinity` no longer immediately disables batching through an invalid attempt count.
